title: Bayer Earnings Beat Estimates on Crop Science Strength
summary: Bayer AG posted better-than-expected profit in the second quarter, helped by a strong performance in its crop science business.

title: India Eyes Up to $3.3 Billion in Insurance Giant Stake Sale
summary: India is aiming to raise as much as $3.3 billion by selling a small stake in Life Insurance Corp. in one of the country’s largest-ever offer-for-sale transactions, as the government seeks to bolster public finances amid challenges posed by high oil prices.

title: Global Stocks Hold Near Record High, Yen Weakens: Markets Wrap
summary: Global stocks held near record highs and futures pointed to further gains after a tech-led Wall Street rally followed a month of high volatility. The yen gave back some of its recent advance that was triggered by US and Japanese intervention.

title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Aug. 4
summary: Oil rose after its biggest drop in a week, as President Donald Trump said his latest offer of talks is Tehran’s “last chance” and that he expects a full reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.

title: Lufthansa Warns of Profit Risk as Jet Fuel Surge Roils Industry
summary: Deutsche Lufthansa AG warned of heightened uncertainty for its full-year outlook as volatility in jet fuel prices and shortened booking cycles complicate efforts to boost profit.

title: South Korea’s Leveraged ETF Trading Plummets Under New Curbs
summary: Trading in leveraged exchange-traded funds tied to South Korea’s two chip giants has shrunk sharply, after authorities took steps to slow demand for the products that fueled recent market volatility.

title: Trump Says Talks Are Iran’s ‘Last Chance’ After Threats
summary: President Donald Trump said his latest offer of talks is a “last chance” for Iran after he called off what he said was a major attack on the Islamic Republic. Bloomberg's Stuart Livingstone-Wallace breaks down the latest developments. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Chinese Dip-Buying Bolsters Gold as Prices Find Floor at $4,000
summary: Chinese institutional investors have swooped on gold in recent weeks, helping to arrest the precious metal’s decline and keep prices above the key threshold of $4,000 an ounce.

title: China Anxious About Mythos Ahead of Trump-Xi Meeting
summary: China is growing anxious that Anthropic’s Mythos could be wielded against the world’s second-biggest economy, adding a volatile new issue to already heightened tensions before a planned summit between Xi Jinping and Donald Trump. Bloomberg's Minmin Low has the latest. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Jefferies' Cui Cui on Wuxi Apptec's Earnings
summary: Jefferies Head of Asia Healthcare Research says the outlook for Wuxi Apptec remains bright. She spoke with "Bloomberg: The China Show" after Wuxi Apptec reported an earnings beat and raised its full year guidance. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Citi Says Japan Has Yen Defense Tools Beyond Treasury Sales
summary: Japan has alternative tools to defend the yen without liquidating its more than $1.1 trillion US Treasury portfolio as its short-term debt holdings run low, according to Citigroup Inc.

title: Japan's Equities Risk Tactical Correction: Goldman's Moe
summary: Goldman Sachs Chief APAC Regional Equity Strategist Timothy Moe discusses Japan's macroeconomic environment following recent currency market intervention, warning that Japanese stocks risk a tactical pullback. However, he notes corporate earnings will likely remain intact and maintains a bullish view on structural market fundamentals. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: India Raises Fuel Export Tax to Build Stocks on War Concerns
summary: India increased levies on exports of oil products to bolster domestic fuel stockpiles while global supplies remained tight despite a pause in fighting between the US and Iran.

title: Rocky Debut for India Closing Auction Sparks Worries Over Expiry
summary: India’s weekly derivatives expiry will be closely watched on Tuesday after a new closing auction system unexpectedly pushed the NSE Nifty 50 Index higher on its first day, raising questions over how the change could affect trading on one of the market’s busiest days.

title: Australia’s Housing Market Worsens
summary: Australia's housing downturn is accelerating, with higher interest rates and weaker investor demand driving the biggest home price declines since late 2022. REA Group Senior Economist Anne Flaherty says further falls are likely through year-end, especially in higher-priced suburbs. She discussed the outlook for Australia's housing market on "Bloomberg: The Asia Trade". (Source: Bloomberg)
